item.title: AI for Good: Ethics, Inclusivity, and Sustainability in Tourism
item.content:encoded:
This curated collection focuses on how artificial intelligence can contribute positively to the tourism industry while addressing critical ethical, inclusivity, and sustainability concerns. The collection seeks research that explores responsible AI implementation across tourism operations, emphasizing fair and unbiased systems, equitable access for diverse stakeholders, and environmental stewardship. The work invites scholars to examine both the opportunities and challenges associated with integrating AI technologies into tourism contexts, particularly regarding their effects on local communities and ecosystems.

Appel publié par Annals of Tourism Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical considerations in AI applications within the tourism sector
  • Inclusive AI systems that serve diverse tourist populations and communities
  • Sustainability applications of AI in tourism operations and planning
  • Responsible innovation and governance frameworks for AI in tourism
  • AI-driven solutions addressing social and environmental challenges in tourism
  • Algorithmic bias and fairness in tourism recommendation systems and services
  • Community engagement and stakeholder perspectives on AI implementation in tourism
  • Long-term impacts of AI adoption on tourism destinations and local economies

Timeline

  • September 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Imagery, Attention and Destination Governance - From imagery to impact: how visual media shape tourism behaviour, space and governance
item.content:encoded:
,

,

This special issue examines how visual media and imagery influence tourism in multiple dimensions. The focus encompasses how visual representations drive tourist decision-making and travel behaviour, how images direct tourist attention and shape experiences, and how visual communication strategies function in marketing destinations.

The collection seeks contributions investigating the governance aspects of tourism imagery, including how visual representations are controlled and shaped by destination management, as well as the role of emerging technologies like augmented and virtual reality in transforming how potential and actual tourists engage with destinations.

Appel publié par Tourism Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Tourist attention and gaze: how visual representations shape what tourists see and experience

item.title: Phygital Well-Being in Hybrid Tourism Destinations: Human-Centric Design, Management, and Visitor Welfare
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the intersection of physical and digital experiences in tourism destinations, focusing on how hybrid environments can be designed and managed to enhance visitor well-being. It seeks research addressing the implementation of human-centered design approaches that effectively blend tangible and virtual tourism elements while prioritizing the welfare of visitors and all stakeholders involved in the destination ecosystem.

item.title: The Impact of the Political Environment on Tourism and Hospitality
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to explore the multifaceted ways in which political environments shape and influence the tourism and hospitality sectors. The political context encompasses governmental policies, political stability, regulatory frameworks, international relations, and geopolitical events that directly and indirectly affect tourism flows, hospitality operations, and industry development.

We invite submissions that examine how political factors influence destination competitiveness, tourism demand and supply, hospitality business strategies, employment patterns, and sustainable development in the sector. We particularly welcome research that addresses contemporary political challenges and opportunities in tourism and hospitality.

Contributions may include empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, case studies, and comparative analyses that provide insights into the complex relationships between political environments and tourism and hospitality industries globally.

Appel publié par Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Tourism and the 2026 Middle East Crisis: International and Regional Implications
item.content:encoded:
C. Michael Hall, Massey University

The ongoing Middle East conflict involving Israel, Iran, the United States, Lebanon, and Palestine represents the most significant disruption to international tourism since COVID-19. Its effects extend globally through disrupted aviation hubs in the Gulf, restricted airspace affecting Asia-Europe travel, and threats to shipping routes, alongside direct threats to tourism infrastructure worldwide.

Beyond direct military impacts, the crisis influences global tourism through elevated oil and energy costs, affecting aviation fuel prices and transport expenses. This energy crisis, reportedly exceeding previous major oil shocks combined, threatens airline viability and has implications for the sustainability and future trajectory of tourism infrastructure and carbon-dependent transport networks.

The journal invites research examining how the crisis affects tourist behavior, destination competitiveness, industry resilience, and government and business responses across international, regional, national, and local contexts, as well as its broader implications for tourism governance and energy futures.

Appel publié par Current Issues in Tourism. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
